title: IV fluid tonicity

findings.where: Images 1, 5, 6, 8, 12 and 13: bag-table row labels; step "bags"; tonicity.jsx LISTS, facts[4] and text alternatives
findings.title: Osmolarity categories are labeled with tonicity terms
findings.problem: The table explicitly classifies in-bag osmolarity but calls its rows "Isotonic," "Hypotonic" and "Hypertonic." That is common nursing shorthand, but it conflicts with this lesson's explicit distinction between osmolarity and tonicity—especially for D5W. The subsequent dextrose explanation is correct; the terminology remains inconsistent.
findings.fix: Use "Approximately iso-osmolar," "Hypo-osmolar" and "Hyperosmolar" for the in-bag categories. If retaining familiar nursing-category names, identify them explicitly as conventional textbook labels rather than definitions of physiologic tonicity. Update the corresponding facts and text alternatives.

assessment: Minor terminology revision needed in the bag-classification section.
